lines.text: [Alaska](/æˈlæskə/) and Alberta both struck it rich selling oil.
[Alaska](/æˈlæskə/) turned it into an eighty-eight-billion-dollar fund.
Alberta's fund is about a quarter of that.
Here's why.
In nineteen seventy-six, Alaskans voted to save part of their oil money.
At least twenty-five percent of oil royalties goes in,
to one giant fund, and those savings can only be invested.
They invested it, and it just kept growing.
Now it pays out about three point eight billion dollars a year, for dividends and public services,
and the fund is still growing.
Alberta went the other way.
It took in about eighteen billion dollars of resource revenue last year alone.
The plan back in nineteen seventy-six?
To save thirty cents of every resource dollar.
And here's the twist.
In nineteen eighty-seven, the deposits stopped.
Not one new dollar went in until two thousand six.
Two places.
Same oil.
[Alaska](/æˈlæskə/) kept saving.
Alberta stopped for nineteen years.
